stories.headline: Iran tensions escalate amid failed US diplomatic efforts
stories.summary: Trump has rejected Iran's response to a U.S. proposal aimed at ending their conflict, calling the Iranian position unacceptable. Oil prices rose following his dismissal, as both sides accuse each other of making demands that undermine peace negotiations.

angles.headline: Trump calls Iran response to US proposal to end war 'totally unacceptable'
angles.summary: Trump has rejected Iran's response to a U.S. proposal aimed at ending their conflict, calling the Iranian position unacceptable. Oil prices rose following his dismissal, as both sides accuse each other of making demands that undermine peace negotiations.

angles.headline: Iran warns Europe against sending warships to Hormuz as US talks gap widens
angles.summary: Iran objects to a proposed European naval mission aimed at protecting merchant ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, viewing it as interference in regional affairs. Britain and France are convening defense ministers to discuss the escort initiative as diplomatic tensions with Iran intensify alongside stalled negotiations with the United States.

angles.headline: Iran executes young aerospace engineer over CIA and Mossad espionage allegations
angles.summary: Iran has executed a young aerospace engineer on charges of espionage for the CIA and Mossad, marking another capital case involving alleged foreign intelligence collaboration. The execution underscores Iran's continued use of espionage allegations as both a security measure and a tool in its broader tensions with the United States and Israel.

stories.headline: British passengers from hantavirus-hit cruise ship isolating in hospital
stories.summary: British passengers from a cruise ship are isolating in a hospital after hantavirus exposure, following cases confirmed among US and French nationals who were aboard the same vessel. The outbreak has prompted the evacuation and hospitalization of multiple passengers, marking a shift in how the facility—which previously managed Covid quarantines—responds to emerging infectious disease threats.

stories.headline: Analysis: Has Starmer done enough to save his premiership?
stories.summary: Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces mounting pressure from within his own Labour party, with some MPs questioning whether his recent pledges to improve performance address the fundamental concerns driving calls for his resignation. His speech and vows have drawn criticism as insufficient from senior party figures, leaving unclear whether he has stabilized his position or merely delayed a reckoning.

stories.headline: Philippines vice president Sara Duterte impeached for a second time
stories.summary: Philippine lawmakers have impeached Vice President Sara Duterte for the second time this year, advancing a case that will proceed to the Senate for trial. The impeachment follows escalating political tensions between Duterte and President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., with supporters and opponents of the vice president holding competing visions for the country's political direction.

stories.headline: Kenya hosts France’s Macron: Why the relationship matters to both
stories.summary: French President Macron visits Kenya to rebuild France's strained relationship with African nations and position Europe as a relevant strategic partner on the continent. The visit reflects France's broader effort to counter its declining influence in Africa amid competition from other global powers and criticism of its colonial legacy.

stories.headline: Nobel laureate’s smuggled memoir details beatings and neglect in Iranian prisons
stories.summary: Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi has documented accounts of beatings and neglect during her imprisonment in Iran, revealing conditions in the country's detention system through a smuggled memoir. Her recent transfer to a Tehran hospital signals an ongoing medical crisis tied to her years of confinement.

stories.headline: Who is Gerhard Schroeder, Putin’s pick for Ukraine peace talks mediation?
stories.summary: Gerhard Schröder, Germany's former chancellor with longstanding ties to Vladimir Putin, has been proposed by the Kremlin as a potential mediator in Ukraine peace negotiations. European Union officials have rejected the suggestion, citing Schröder's close relationship with Putin as incompatible with impartial mediation.

stories.headline: Thailand’s former PM Thaksin Shinawatra released from jail
stories.summary: Thaksin Shinawatra walks free after serving eight months of a prison sentence for financial crimes, marking a significant shift in Thai politics after years of exile and legal battles. His release comes as rivals remain entrenched in government, leaving unclear what political role the influential former leader will pursue next.

stories.headline: Body of missing US soldier recovered off coast of Morocco
stories.summary: Moroccan authorities have recovered the body of a U.S. soldier who went missing during military exercises in the country. The discovery comes as search efforts continue for a second soldier who remains unaccounted for.

stories.headline: Portrait looted by Nazis found in home of Dutch SS leader's descendants
stories.summary: A portrait looted during the Nazi era has been discovered in the home of descendants belonging to a Dutch SS leader who collaborated with Nazi Germany. The artwork, originally taken from a Jewish collector, surfaced through the investigation of an art researcher focused on recovering Nazi-looted cultural property.
